answers.question: Is crime rising or falling in Bernal Heights, San Francisco (past year vs the year before, as of mid-2026)?
answers.answer: Crime is falling in Bernal Heights. Victim-reported crime — the best measure of what residents actually experience — dropped about 43% (877 vs 1,532 incidents), a statistically notable decline (z ≈ -2.1). Total crime incidents also fell 32%, and this isn't explained by reduced policing, since enforcement activity stayed essentially flat (+1.5%).

answers.question: 311 noise complaints in San Francisco rose over 60% in the year to mid-2026. Does that mean the city actually got dramatically louder?
answers.answer: No — a 60%+ jump in 311 noise complaints measures reporting behavior, not decibels. The increase is nearly citywide (complaints rose in ~35 of 40 neighborhoods, including quiet areas like Noe Valley and West of Twin Peaks), which is the classic signature of a reporting or platform change — like an app update, outreach campaign, or a few prolific complainers — rather than the whole city suddenly getting louder. That said, a few localized spikes may reflect real changes: Mission Bay (+164%), Western Addition (+193%), Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside (+215%), and the Tenderloin (+133%) are statistical outliers (z > 1.2) that could indicate genuine new noise sources like construction or nightlife. Meanwhile, North Beach complaints actually fell 26%, so if quiet matters to you, look at the neighborhood-level outliers rather than the headline citywide number.
